story.title: Two Men Charged in Connection with RAF Fairford Incident Linked to Iranian Intelligence
story.summary: Two British men have been charged with national security offenses related to an incident at RAF Fairford, a U.S. military base, which occurred in September. Authorities suspect that the incident may involve Iranian state involvement, with one of the suspects accused of assisting Iranian intelligence.

event_overview.title: About Terrorism Investigation
event_overview.subject: Terrorism Investigation
event_overview.summary: This is an ongoing UK counter-terrorism and national-security investigation into suspicious vehicle activity reported near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire on 27 September 2026. The inquiry began with arrests on suspicion of explosives and terrorism-preparation offences; by 27 October, prosecutors had charged two men under the National Security Act 2023, while Counter Terrorism Policing said its investigation remained live and that it believed the relevant foreign intelligence service was Iranian.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: Police received a report at about 12:45 a.m. on 27 September 2026 concerning three suspicious vehicles apparently travelling toward RAF Fairford. As of 27 October 2026, the investigation and associated criminal proceedings were ongoing.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The incident was near RAF Fairford and Whelford in Gloucestershire, England. RAF Fairford is owned by the UK government and used by the US Air Force as a bomber forward operating base.

facts.label: Investigating and prosecuting bodies
facts.value: Counter Terrorism Policing is leading the investigation, working with Gloucestershire Police and other partners; the Crown Prosecution Service authorized the two charges announced on 27 October 2026.

facts.label: Initial legal basis
facts.value: The first five arrests were on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and of preparing terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006. Section 5 covers conduct in preparation for committing, or assisting another to commit, acts of terrorism.

facts.label: Charges as of 27 October
facts.value: Two men were charged under sections 3 and 4 of the National Security Act 2023: one with assisting a foreign intelligence service and one with entering, inspecting or approaching a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to UK safety or interests. These are allegations for a court to determine, not findings of guilt.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers major publicly reported arrests, bail decisions and charges in the RAF Fairford investigation from 27 September through 27 October 2026; it does not attempt to document every police action, court step, or wider UK-Iran security development.

explore_lenses.label: What was found near RAF Fairford?
explore_lenses.title: No improvised explosives were found
explore_lenses.summary: The September 27 response began after reports of three suspicious vehicles near RAF Fairford. Police later said examinations found petrol but no improvised explosive devices, separating the confirmed physical evidence from the still-unresolved alleged intent.

claims.text: Counter Terrorism Policing says armed officers arrested five men after a report at about 12:45 a.m. on September 27 that three vehicles were travelling toward the air base.
After examining the vehicles with military and forensic support, police said no improvised explosive devices were found, although a quantity of petrol was recovered.
The initial security operation included a 400-metre cordon and precautionary evacuation of about 85 households while Army explosive-ordnance specialists examined the vehicles.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case develop into these charges?
explore_lenses.title: The allegations cover activity before the September alert
explore_lenses.summary: The two National Security Act charges are distinct and concern alleged activity spanning August and September, not simply the events at the roadside scene on September 27. Police say their Iran assessment emerged from a continuing evidence review, rather than from a public disclosure of the underlying evidence.

claims.text: The CPS alleges that Nouman Essghir inspected, approached, or was near a prohibited place on August 22 for a purpose prejudicial to UK safety or interests; it alleges that Mohmed Abdulkarim assisted a foreign intelligence service in UK-related activity between August 31 and September 28.
Police say Essghir was first arrested near RAF Fairford on September 27 and re-arrested on October 20; detectives subsequently interviewed Abdulkarim under caution before charging him.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said police believe the foreign country relevant to Abdulkarim's charge is Iran, while describing the broader inquiry as one in which investigators are still examining the level of state involvement and the intended objective.

Section 3 of the National Security Act covers conduct likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in UK-related activities; examples in the statute include providing information, goods, services, or financial benefits.

explore_lenses.title: Court proceedings begin as the investigation continues
explore_lenses.summary: Both defendants were scheduled for their first Westminster Magistrates' Court hearing on October 27. Separately, the police investigation remains active, with other people arrested in the inquiry still on bail; no further diplomatic or base-operational step has been officially announced in the sources reviewed.

claims.text: The CPS said the first hearing for Abdulkarim and Essghir would take place at Westminster Magistrates' Court on October 27, 2026, and stressed that charges are not findings of guilt.

Counter Terrorism Policing says five other men arrested in connection with the RAF Fairford investigation remain on police bail; a 25-year-old dual UK-Iranian national re-arrested on October 20 was released without charge but remains on bail from his earlier arrest.

RAF Fairford is the U.S. Air Force's preferred bomber forward operating location in Europe, according to the 501st Combat Support Wing, which explains the base's strategic relevance but does not establish the alleged plot's objective.

story_report.summary: British nationals Nouman Essghir and Mohmed Abdulkarim have been charged under national-security legislation following an investigation into an incident near RAF Fairford, a U.S. military base. Prosecutors allege Essghir acted in relation to a prohibited place, while Abdulkarim is accused of assisting a foreign intelligence service in UK-related activity. Police say they believe the foreign country relevant to Abdulkarim’s charge is Iran, though investigators are still assessing the extent of any state involvement and the intended objective. Their first hearing was scheduled for Westminster Magistrates’ Court on October 27, 2026.

sections.heading: Police response near RAF Fairford
sections.body: Armed officers arrested five men after a report at about 12:45 a.m. on September 27 that three vehicles were travelling toward RAF Fairford. Police imposed a 400-metre cordon and evacuated about 85 households as Army explosive-ordnance specialists examined the vehicles. Investigators said no improvised explosive devices were found, although they recovered a quantity of petrol.

sections.heading: Allegations under National Security Act
sections.body: The Crown Prosecution Service alleges Essghir inspected, approached or was near a prohibited place on August 22 for a purpose prejudicial to UK safety or interests. It alleges Abdulkarim assisted a foreign intelligence service in UK-related activity between August 31 and September 28. Under Section 3 of the National Security Act, conduct that is likely materially to assist a foreign intelligence service can include providing information, goods, services or financial benefits; the charges are not findings of guilt.

sections.heading: RAF Fairford’s strategic role
sections.body: RAF Fairford is the U.S. Air Force’s preferred bomber forward operating location in Europe, according to the 501st Combat Support Wing. Five other men arrested in connection with the investigation remain on police bail. A 25-year-old dual UK-Iranian national who was re-arrested on October 20 was released without charge, while remaining on bail from his earlier arrest.

related_stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Surpasses 10,000 Cases Amid Growing Concerns
related_stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has exceeded 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly 4,900 reported deaths. This outbreak, driven by the Bundibugyo virus, is noted as the fastest-growing in history, raising alarms about potential spread to other African nations. Currently, there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments available for this strain of the virus.
